events.region: Dona Ana, NM; Otero, NM; El Paso, TX
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Dona Ana County in south central New Mexico...
Southwestern Otero County in south central New Mexico...
Northwestern El Paso County in western Texas...

* Until 545 PM MDT.

* At 410 PM MDT, Torrential rain showers have been moving north
across the lower Mesilla Valley, the west slopes of the Franklin
Mountains, and portions of the far southern Tularosa Basin. The
heaviest rainfall has been just east of Berino, Anthony, Vinton,
and Canutillo.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of arroyos, urban areas, highways, streets
and underpasses as well as other poor drainage and
low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Northwest El Paso, Chaparral, Anthony, Vado, Anthony Gap, Berino,
Canutillo, Westway, Vinton and Mesquite.

Arroyos and low water crossings in Franklin Mountains State Park may
become too dangerous to cross, including in the Tom Mays Unit.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Sierra County in south central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Arroyos and washes continue to rise due to excess runoff
from earlier rainfall. Low-water crossings are inundated with water
and may not be passable. Expect many areas of slow moving or
standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 359 PM MDT, A broad area of moderate to locally heavy rainfall
continues to lift across the region. Expect flooding to continue
into the evening hours. Urban flooding in poor drainage areas,
and widespread flooding of low lying areas in the Jornada del
Muerto can be expected.
- This replaces the Flash Flood Warning that was set to expire at 4
PM.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Upham, Cuchillo, Truth or Consequences, Engle, Cutter, City of
Elephant Butte, Palomas, Spaceport America, Williamsburg, Alamosa
Canyon and Elephant Butte Lake.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Streams continue to rise due to excess runoff from
earlier rainfall. Expect many areas of slow moving or standing
water. It will take several hours for all the water from these
storms to work through local drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 253 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in McClellan Wash.
- An automated stream gauge located at McClellan Wash and the CAP
Canal reported a stage of 11.5 feet. At 12 feet, flooding is
possible downstream in the town of Picacho and Eloy.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Picacho and Eloy.
- This includes the following highways...
Route 87 between mile markers 116 and 117. Interstate 10 between
mile markers 212 and 221.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San
Pablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Now through 5 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.03 ft MLLW) at 2:10 PM
Wednesday 9/30, and 1.1 ft above normal (6.92 ft MLLW) at 2:58
PM Thursday 10/01. These predictions include up to 0.7 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

events.summary:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Otero County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 645 PM MDT.

* At 352 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms with torrential rainfall over parts of the southern
Sacramento Mountains. Rainfall rates of 2 to 3 inches per hour have
been observed. The heaviest rainfall has been in the area of Bug
Scuffle to near Sacramento Lake South of Sunspot, and at the head
of Hay Canyon and Agua Chiquita Creek.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, roads, as well
as other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Timberon, Sacramento, Sunspot, Mayhill, Weed, Hay Canyon, Cox
Canyon, Benson Ridge, Miller Flats, McDonald Flats and Lower Dry
Burnt Canyon.

Flooding is likely to occur on the Sacramento River in and near
Timberon, and Agua Chiquita Creek above Sacramento.
